text: Council — the tour master of the estate Council · the signed visual mind · 2026-08-06 The tour master reads newest-first. Every measurement this estate signs becomes a card under 3 KB — score, n, interval, provenance. Cards supersede; the newest card is the current truth; the older ones stay auditable. Council is the surface that reads that timeline from the top — 13 greenfield axes, the router's measured routes, and the algebra that guarantees the read always converges to the same state, in any order, on any machine. 13 greenfield axes on the board 12 with measured banks 2 quotable axes (n ≥ 30, interval carried) 2 measured router routes, opposite directions 4/4 algebra laws hold on the real cards <3 KB per signed card, budget enforced The 13 axes — one card each, glyphs derived from card content Gold border = quotable (n ≥ 30 with interval). Cyan = measured bank, runs pending or interval not yet quotable. Red = correctly silent — an empty lane published as empty. Scores are macro-F1 with Wilson 95% intervals where carried. The router — two measured routes, opposite directions "Route each task to the family that owns it" stopped being a slogan when the second route was measured. The small sovereign classifier owns injection detection; the frontier owns hard reasoning. The router picks neither favourite — it reads the card and sends the task to the measured winner. task family sovereign small frontier comparator separation route → prompt-injection detection recall 1.000 [0.938, 1.000] 200 KB TF-IDF · 0.065 ms/text · CPU gpt-4o-mini 0.793 [0.672, 0.877] disjoint intervals McNemar p = 4.9×10⁻⁴ (12–0) sovereign small (n = 80) hard reasoning (arithmetic) 0/11 — no arithmetic ability 11/11 = 1.000 [0.741, 1.000] total separation frontier (n = 11) The injection separation holds on one corpus (deepset prompt-injection, held out; 0 of 546 training rows overlap). Wider corpora are the next measurement, not an assumption. Toxicity, semantic-novelty and containment lanes are published as empty — no figure without a run. The card algebra — measured, not asserted Tested against the real 12-card board, not argued from analogy. The card knowledge-base is a CRDT-like commutative monoid : the same formal property distributed databases use to guarantee consistency without a coordinator — which is exactly what a sovereign, federated estate needs. ✓ Associative. Combining cards A then B then C equals A with (B then C) — merge grouping never changes the outcome. ✓ Idempotent. Re-merging an already-included card changes nothing — newest-supersedes is a safe update, replays are harmless. ✓ Timestamp-commutative & order-convergent. Any read or merge order reaches the identical final state. This is the formal guarantee behind "read newest-first and always land on the same truth". ✓ Valid metric space. 0 of 1,728 triangle-inequality checks violated — the GNN/clustering layer is mathematically grounded, and scores are totally ordered. The boundary that keeps this honest: the algebra governs how cards combine — it cannot derive a measurement. You cannot algebra your way to a model's score; you still run the harness. Math applies to structure, convergence and embedding — never to generating the numbers.
